construction_year_audit.scope: All 29 directory entries with year_built null at the start of this audit; the 326 existing years were not re-audited.

methodology.researchers: One dedicated sub-agent per building/community, followed by parent review and targeted follow-up on conflicting evidence.
methodology.identity: Match addresses, former names, parcels, building counts and phases before using a year.
methodology.source_priority: Prefer direct assessor, permit, owner/developer, architect and contractor evidence; corroborate with contemporary reporting and property listings. Syndicated listings are not assumed independent.
methodology.date_interpretation: Record an evidenced original construction or completion year; distinguish construction starts, forecasts, effective years, renovations, opening, and permit closeout. Material differences remain documented.
methodology.multiple_buildings: Identify explicitly which building or phase the scalar year describes. Original community phases may be recorded with later phases noted. At the user's request, The Magnolia Collection uses its oldest constituent building's construction year, with the other buildings documented separately.
methodology.access_limits: Evidence notes identify search-index-only or indirectly cited material when direct source access was unavailable.

results.name: 2nd and John
results.rationale: Recommend 2019 as the best-supported year for overall building completion. The developer's completed-projects page says Completed 2019, and its owner-side partner Westminster says the 80-unit building was completed and sold in 2019. Contemporaneous 2019 reporting calls it recently completed and says it opened in January. Several exact-address listings and a sales-comps table report 2018, and the framing contractor's portfolio also says completed 2018. Those are material contradictions; available sources do not establish whether the 2018 value reflects a different completion definition or a reporting error. Weight the developer/owner's explicit completion statements for this field, with medium confidence because the contradiction remains unresolved.

sources.note: Primary developer's completed-projects page identifies '2nd+John Apartments,' 80 units, Queen Anne, and says 'Completed 2019.' This is the developer's explicit overall completion statement.
Owner-side partner portfolio lists '2nd and John Apartments, Seattle, WA,' partner Continental Properties LLC, and says the 80-unit rental building was 'completed and sold in 2019.'

Republished Puget Sound Business Journal article dated August 14, 2019 states Continental sold a 'recently completed 80-unit apartment building' in Lower Queen Anne; it identifies 'The 2nd & John building (200 Second Ave. W.)' and says it 'opened in January' and was about 97% leased. The article does not independently specify when construction completion occurred, but supports 2019 operational completion.

Commercial apartment sales appraisal, PDF p. 107 (printed p. 109), lists the 2019 sale entry: 2nd & John; 200 2ND AVE W; 2018; 80 units; 55,010 building SF; $40,000,000 sale. This is direct exact-address evidence for 2018 but conflicts with project stakeholders' explicit 2019 completion statements.
Listing identifies 2nd and John at 200 2nd Ave W, Seattle, WA 98119 and states under Property Information: 'Built in 2018' and '80 units/7 stories.'

JRT Northwest's project portfolio identifies '2nd & John,' Seattle, GC Compass Construction, and 'Completed: 2018.' JRT is a wood-framing contractor; the page does not disclose its work scope or say whether this date is final whole-building completion.

Seattle Daily Journal of Commerce interview published February 22, 2018 says Continental Properties' 80-unit 2nd and John project on Lower Queen Anne 'will finish in December.' This is a forecast, not a report of actual completion.
RentCafe listing at 200 2nd Ave. W states '1 buildings in the community 80 apartments in the community 7 stories per building Building constructed in 2019.'

Kidder Mathews offering memorandum lists 2ND & JOHN at 200 2nd Ave W as a 2019 year-built rent comparable. It is a broker marketing document and conflicts with the 2018 year-built value in another commercial sales report.

King County Department of Assessments 2025 Apartment Specialty report maps parcel 198920-0880 to 200 2ND AVE W (p. 59). This confirms the assessor parcel for the subject property; the report does not state its year built.

notes: The apartments.json record is id 2nd-and-john, name 2nd and John, address 200 2nd Ave W, Seattle, WA 98119; it describes one 80-unit property and no separate phases.

The developer's explicit 2019 completion statement is corroborated by its owner-side partner, and contemporaneous August 2019 reporting says the exact-address building opened in January and had recently been completed.

Exact-address commercial and apartment listings report year built 2018, and the framing contractor portfolio says completed 2018. Available sources do not establish whether this refers to the whole building or another reporting definition, so that distinction is not assumed.
King County's 2025 apartment-specialty report identifies parcel 198920-0880 at 200 2nd Ave W; it does not provide a construction year. No exact certificate-of-occupancy date was obtained.
conflicts: 2019 overall completion: Continental Properties' official completed-projects page says Completed 2019; owner-side Westminster Management says the 80-unit building was completed and sold in 2019; and a contemporaneous 2019 report calls it recently completed, identifies 200 Second Ave. W., and says it opened in January.

2018: JRT Northwest's framing-contractor portfolio says completed 2018; Apartments.com says Built in 2018 at the exact address; and a 2019 apartment-sales appraisal table lists the exact address with year built 2018. The sources do not resolve whether the 2018 contractor completion is whole-building completion or a different milestone.
Other commercial and rental sources also conflict: the Kidder Mathews offering memorandum and RentCafe list 2019 as year built/construction year.
research_steps: Read the apartments.json record and confirmed the current name, previous name, exact address, and 80-unit property scope.
Searched exact address and project-name variants ('2nd and John', '2nd & John', and '2nd+John') for developer, contractor, public-record, completion, and property-listing evidence.

Reviewed the developer's completed-projects and news pages, owner-side Westminster portfolio, Seattle DJC reporting, contractor portfolio, contemporaneous 2019 sale/opening report, exact-address apartment listings, and commercial real-estate reports.
Cross-checked parcel identity against King County's assessor report (parcel 198920-0880) and checked Seattle project references; no exact occupancy-certificate date was obtained.

Weighed the developer and owner-side explicit overall completion statements over conflicting year-built aggregator/report entries; retained 2018 evidence and left its relationship to overall completion unresolved.
directory_notes: Construction year uses the developer and owner partner's 2019 completion statements. Some exact-address listings and sales records report 2018; that discrepancy remains documented in the audit.

results.name: 3030 Lake City
results.rationale: 3030 Lake City is the current 113-unit community formerly identified in public records and sales material as Sherwood Apartments. King County Assessor parcel records show the community is phased across two parcels: the 85-unit Sherwood B-E group at 3101 NE 145th St was built in 1975, while the 28-unit Building A at the record's exact address, 3030 NE 143rd St, was built in 1977 (effective year 2000). The 2018 sale-analysis row for the full 113-unit Sherwood community reports 1975, matching the earliest and majority phase. Use 1975 for the community-level record; if the field is intended to describe only the 3030-address Building A, its assessor year is 1977.

sources.note: King County Assessor eReal Property record for parcel 766370-0330 identifies 3101 NE 145th St as SHERWOOD APTS (BLDGS B, C, D, & E), lists 85 units, and gives Year Built 1975. Direct record page reviewed; this is the majority phase of the 113-unit complex.

King County Assessor record for parcel 766370-0369 matches the exact dataset address, 3030 NE 143rd St, and labels it SHERWOOD APTS- BLDG A - 28 UNITS. Building Year Built is 1977; Eff. Year is 2000, which is an effective/renovation year rather than original construction. Direct record page reviewed.

Colliers Seattle Multifamily Team 2019 market-study sales table lists Sherwood at 3030 NE 143rd St as built 1975 with 113 units (sale dated 2018-02-15), matching the full community size. Evidence was available as the search-indexed PDF table text; the PDF page image was not separately inspected, so treat this as snippet/text-extraction evidence.

notes: The property's King County assessor records show multiple construction vintages: the exact-address Building A is 1977, while the 85-unit B-E phase at 3101 NE 145th St is 1975. The current 3030 Lake City offering covers the full 113-unit community, so 1975 is recorded as the community's original/earliest construction year.

Seattle's 2012 and 2015 Energy Benchmarking inventories list Sherwood Building A at 3030 NE 143rd and B-E at 3101 NE 145th, confirming the split-campus identity; these inventories are identity evidence, not year evidence.
The assessor's 2000 effective year for Building A should not be substituted for its 1977 construction year.

conflicts.note: Realtor.com lists 1963 for the current 3030 Lake City page and identifies the listing data as Zillow-provided. This conflicts with the parcel-specific King County assessment and 2018 multifamily sales analysis; lower confidence than those sources.

research_steps: Read apartments.json and matched id 3030-lake-city to 3030 NE 143rd St, Seattle, WA 98125.
Checked King County Assessor eReal Property for parcel 766370-0369 at the exact address: Sherwood Building A, 28 units, Year Built 1977, Eff. Year 2000.
Checked King County Assessor eReal Property for parcel 766370-0330 at 3101 NE 145th St: Sherwood B-E phase, 85 units, Year Built 1975.
Cross-referenced Seattle OSE energy-benchmarking inventories, which identify the two Sherwood addresses as Building A and Buildings B-E.
Compared the 2018 Colliers multifamily sales-analysis row for 3030 NE 143rd: Sherwood, 113 units, Year Built 1975, with the 85+28 assessor unit counts.

Investigated third-party year claims: Compass reports 1977 for the exact-address parcel, consistent with assessor Building A; Realtor.com/Zillow-derived listing reports 1963 and conflicts with the assessor and full-community sale analysis.
directory_notes: The 113-unit community, formerly Sherwood Apartments, spans two construction phases: 85 units at 3101 NE 145th St were built in 1975; the 28-unit Building A at 3030 NE 143rd St was built in 1977. The recorded 1975 is the original community year, not the year of every building.

results.name: Bell Overlake
results.rationale: Recommend 2019 under the dataset rule of original construction/completion year. Strong property-specific evidence identifies 3040 Apartments (the community later renamed Bell Overlake) at 3040 148th Ave NE as completed/delivered in 2019: its architect lists WHEN 2019; Kidder Mathews includes it in its Q2 2019 completed-construction reporting with June 2019 delivery; and contemporaneous September 2019 reporting describes it as recently completed / about three months old. Construction was underway by 2017: Yardi Matrix/Berkadia's 3Q 2017 multifamily pipeline lists Redmond 148 at the exact address as Under Construction, with a March 1, 2017 permit date. A later 2018 Yardi Matrix pipeline still listed it Under Construction and forecast completion in September 2018; the 2019 pipeline lists it in Lease-Up, with forecast completion June 30, 2019 and rent-up beginning March 8, 2019. Separate address-level property records and an apartment-sale appraisal table explicitly report Year Built 2017. Those are real conflicting recorded year-built values; the sources do not explain why they differ. Given the dataset's completion-year convention and direct evidence of 2019 completion, use 2019 and preserve the 2017 record as a conflict.

sources.note: Primary architect Jensen Davenport Architects project page titled The Bell Overlake Apartments. It identifies the project as multifamily in Redmond and gives WHEN as 2019. This is direct year-level completion evidence.

Kidder Mathews Q2 2019 Seattle multifamily research lists 3040 Apartments at 3040 148th Ave NE, Overlake, with 243 units and a June 2019 delivery date in its completed-construction reporting. The old project name, exact address, and unit count match Bell Overlake.

Berkadia's 3Q 2017 Seattle New Construction and Proposed Multifamily Projects map, sourced to Yardi Matrix, lists Redmond 148 at 3040 148th Avenue NE as Under Construction; its permit-date field is 03/01/2017. Confirms the project was underway in 2017; a permit date is not itself a certificate of completion.

Berkadia/Yardi Matrix's 2018 multifamily pipeline still lists Redmond 148 at the exact address as Under Construction, with permit date 03/01/2017 and forecast completion 09/30/2018. This distinguishes the 2017 construction timeline from the later actual completion evidence.

Berkadia/Yardi Matrix's 2Q 2019 pipeline lists 3040 at 3040 148th Avenue NE as Lease-Up, with forecast completion 06/30/2019 and rent-up starting 03/08/2019. This supports the 2019 completion/lease-up period; dates are pipeline fields, so the retrospective completed-construction and contemporaneous sources are stronger for completion.

CoStar News on September 24, 2019 calls the property a three-month-old apartment building, independently implying completion around June 2019. The story is paywalled; the date and sentence are visible on the page/snippet, so this is snippet-visible corroboration.
Seattle DJC on September 20, 2019 describes the six-story, 243-unit Bell Overlake at 3040 148th Ave NE as recently completed. Subscriber-content preview/snippet evidence only.

The exact address-level public-record property page reports Year built 2017, including in its listing-information field. This corroborates the separate 2017 reported year-built record but does not establish 2017 completion.

The 2017 evidence establishes the construction timeline (listed Under Construction with a March 2017 permit date), while 2019 evidence addresses completion/delivery. Do not carry the permit/start year into a field defined as original completion year.

The records do not explain the discrepancy, so retain it explicitly; for this dataset's original construction/completion-year convention, the recommended value is 2019.

results.name: Boardwalk Kirkland

Opened Boardwalk listing at 434 Kirkland Way; Building details say 'Building constructed in 2022.' Rental portal evidence, not a primary record.

results.name: Fremont Village
results.rationale: Recommend 2024 for the current 93-unit Fremont Village replacement building at 4316 Fremont Ave N. The project architect identifies Fremont Village as completed in 2024; a Seattle project tracker gives a specific completion date of July 23, 2024; and Zillow plus a March 2024 Westlake Associates rent-comparables flyer independently label the exact-address building as built in 2024. The 2023 evidence is real but largely records construction activity, a forecasted late-2023 completion/lease-up, or the property's reported opening; those can precede the project's documented final completion date. Confidence is below high because rental listings also report 2023 and secondary property-data portals report 2022. The 1923 year in Seattle seismic records refers to the demolished pre-project commercial building at the same address, not the current apartment building.

sources.note: Primary project architect page: Fremont Village project status is 'Completed in 2024'; it describes a mixed-use building with 93 residential units and one commercial unit. The page's project identity matches Fremont Village, though its extracted page text does not show the street address.

Project page for 4316 Fremont Ave N says the proposal was a five-story, 93-unit apartment building replacing existing buildings, then records 'July 23, 2024: Completed.' This is a third-party tracker of the Seattle project, not a City-hosted record.
Current Fremont Village Apartments listing gives the exact address 4316 Fremont Ave N and says the building was built in 2024.
Commercial real-estate broker's 2024 rent-comparables table lists FREMONT VILLAGE, 4316 Fremont Ave N, year built 2024. It is direct exact-address evidence but a secondary market source.

Exact-address Fremont Village rental listing says year built 2024 and identifies the data as provided by Zillow, so it is corroboration of the Zillow property record but not an independent data lineage.

Exact-address rental community listing says the community was built in 2023 and has five stories and 93 units. It identifies AGM Real Estate Group as manager; this is a direct conflicting property-listing claim.

July 24, 2024 article quotes Fremont Village property manager Gerry Ohrazda and says the Seattle property opened the previous year (2023). This supports a 2023 opening/occupancy date, which may precede recorded project completion.

Q3 2023 multifamily pipeline lists 4316 Fremont Avenue North (93 units) as under construction, forecasting completion on Nov. 30, 2023, rent-up from Dec. 1, 2023, and first move-in Jan. 1, 2024. These are forecast dates, not a record of actual completion.

Construction subcontractor's project page states that its team was installing brick veneer at Fremont Village Apartments in 2023. This establishes active construction during 2023, not the completion year.

Snippet-only secondary property-record evidence shows a 4316 Fremont Ave N entry with 37,584 sqft and built 2022, in addition to a separate 1967 entry. The page's duplicate address entries and conflicting sqft/year make this unsuitable as the sole year source.

Snippet/page text labels 4316 Fremont Ave N as built in 2022, but misclassifies it as a 55,082-sq-ft single-family home. Likely assessor-feed or property-profile metadata; treat as a conflicting low-reliability year claim for this apartment project.

Washington State Ecology's SEPA record identifies the 2020 project at 4316 Fremont Ave N and says the existing buildings were to be demolished for a five-story apartment project. This distinguishes the present building from the earlier address record.

Seattle's June 2024 confirmed unreinforced-masonry list still labels 4316 Fremont Ave N as a one-story commercial building built in 1923. This concerns the former building at this address; it conflicts with the new project's identity only if address-level records are mistaken for the current building.

notes: The current apartments project is variously described as a 93-unit, five-story replacement building; the original April 2020 SEPA proposal described 101 units, while the later 93-unit proposal and completed project better match today's rental property.

The old structure's 1923 year is retained in Seattle's URM lists even though the 2020 permit review described existing buildings to be demolished. Do not copy 1923 onto the current Fremont Village apartment record.

The project may have begun lease-up or admitted tenants in late 2023 while final completion was recorded in 2024. The year recommendation follows documented project completion and current year-built listings.
conflicts: 2023: Apartment Finder (AGM-managed listing) reports the 93-unit, five-story community was built in 2023. A July 2024 article quotes the on-site property manager saying it opened in 2023. Berkadia's Q3 2023 report forecast late-2023 completion and January 2024 first move-in; that forecast is not actual completion evidence.

2022: CountyOffice and Trulia property-profile results show 2022 at the same address. These secondary records describe different parcel/property characteristics (including a 55,082-sq-ft single-family home in Trulia and duplicated entries in CountyOffice), so they appear less reliable for dating this 93-unit apartment project.

1923: Seattle's URM source records the previous one-story commercial building at 4316 Fremont Ave N as built in 1923. The 2020 SEPA record says existing buildings would be demolished, so 1923 applies to the former structure, not Fremont Village.
research_steps: Read the apartments.json record and confirmed the target is Fremont Village, id fremont-village, at 4316 Fremont Ave N, Seattle, WA 98103.

results.name: Kirkland Crossing
